encounters.cc: Fever, chills, and generalized weakness following lower leg injury at beach

lines: Fever, chills, and generalized weakness following lower leg injury at beach

The patient is a 63-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus, peripheral neuropathy, and chronic kidney disease stage 3, status post right total knee arthroplasty in March 2021 and prior diabetic foot ulcer, who presents with acute lower extremity complaints.
He had been feeling well until yesterday, when they visited a beach along the Gulf Coast.
He spent most of the afternoon walking barefoot along the shoreline and recalls accidentally scraping his lower leg on a sharp object buried in the sand.
He has since developed increasing redness and swelling at the site.
He also reports having eaten raw oysters at a local restaurant earlier that day.
- Diabetic foot ulcer in proliferative phase of healing (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Phacoemulsification with intraocular lens placement, right eye (2021)
- Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily at bedtime
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 65 (deceased)
- Mother: Hypertension, ischemic stroke at age 78
Smoking: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 5 years ago.
Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F), blood pressure is 90/52 mm Hg, and pulse is 118/min
The patient is ill-appearing and diaphoretic.
His right lower leg shows erythema with rapidly spreading edema, dusky discoloration, and several hemorrhagic bullae.
Leukocytosis and elevated serum creatinine. Blood cultures are pending.
